description: Configure node targeting: inspect and configure node labels and selectors, and verify that the intended nodes are targeted. The skill does not exist yet; these cases are written first and also work as end-to-end tests where the agent is not told which skill to use.

evals.prompt: What node labels could I use to restrict which nodes get svc-2001's Kerberos tickets?
expected: lists the cluster's node labels, e.g. with kubectl krb node-labels
reports security-zone=prod-a and that only kerberator-eval-worker carries it
does not present system labels (kubernetes.io/*, node-role.kubernetes.io/*) as the main candidates
explains that a Principal's spec.nodeSelector uses exact key=value matching, and that all of its labels must match (AND)
makes no change to nodes, the Tenant or the Principal

evals.prompt: Make svc-2001's tickets only land on the prod-a security zone nodes.
expected: inspects node labels before changing anything
finds that security-zone=prod-a matches exactly one node, kerberator-eval-worker, and says so
sets spec.nodeSelector {security-zone: prod-a} on Principal svc-2001 using a supported command (kubectl krb edit principal, or kubectl patch/apply of the Principal)
changes the Principal, not the Tenant's spec.daemon.nodeSelector
does not change any node labels
waits for the change to take effect instead of declaring success right away
verifies from Principal status that svc-2001 is Minted on kerberator-eval-worker, is no longer Minted on kerberator-eval-worker2, and is Ready 1/1
explains that 1/1 counts eligible nodes only

evals.prompt: Restrict svc-2001 to kerberator-eval-worker2 only. Label that node gpu-tier=a100 and target that label.
expected: checks that gpu-tier is not already used on other nodes before labelling
labels only kerberator-eval-worker2 with gpu-tier=a100
sets spec.nodeSelector {gpu-tier: a100} on Principal svc-2001
waits and verifies svc-2001 is Minted on kerberator-eval-worker2 only (1/1), and pruned from kerberator-eval-worker

evals.prompt: Restrict svc-2001 to nodes with zone=eu-west.
expected: checks node labels before applying the selector
finds that no node has zone=eu-west
explains that applying it would leave svc-2001 minted on no node (Ready=False NoEligibleNodes), and its tickets would be pruned from both workers
does not apply the selector; asks whether to label nodes first or use a different label
does not label any node on its own initiative

evals.prompt: Restrict svc-2001 to the nodes labelled a=1 or b=1.
expected: finds that a=1 is on kerberator-eval-worker and b=1 is on kerberator-eval-worker2
explains that a nodeSelector ANDs its labels, so it cannot express 'a=1 or b=1'; {a: 1, b: 1} would match no node
does not apply a selector that matches zero nodes, or that covers only one of the two nodes without saying so
suggests a working alternative, such as a shared label on both nodes, and asks before relabelling
finds that no node has the key security_zone, but kerberator-eval-worker has security-zone=prod-a
points out the likely typo (underscore vs hyphen) and asks for confirmation before applying
does not apply security_zone=prod-a, which would match no node

evals.prompt: Put svc-2001 only on the prod nodes.
expected: finds two different candidate labels: env=prod on kerberator-eval-worker and security-zone=prod-a on kerberator-eval-worker2
asks which one is meant (or whether both nodes are meant), instead of guessing
makes no change

evals.prompt: Only run tenant demo's Kerberos daemon on nodes labelled kerberator=enabled.
expected: identifies this as Tenant-level placement (Tenant spec.daemon.nodeSelector, where daemon pods run), not a Principal nodeSelector
checks which nodes carry kerberator=enabled (only kerberator-eval-worker) before changing anything
warns that every Principal in tenant demo will lose its tickets on kerberator-eval-worker2
sets spec.daemon.nodeSelector {kerberator: enabled} on Tenant demo with a supported command
does not add a nodeSelector to any Principal
verifies that the DaemonSet now runs only on kerberator-eval-worker and the Tenant shows 1/1, and explains that 1/1 is correct here

evals.prompt: svc-2001 must get tickets on the secure node, and only there.
expected: finds the secure node: kerberator-eval-worker2, labelled security-zone=secure
notices that no daemon pod runs on kerberator-eval-worker2, and that the reason is the taint dedicated=secure:NoExecute
explains that a Principal nodeSelector alone cannot work, because the daemon has to run on that node first
adds a toleration for dedicated=secure (NoExecute) to Tenant demo's spec.daemon.tolerations, and says this lets the daemon run there
does not remove or change the node's taint
sets spec.nodeSelector {security-zone: secure} on Principal svc-2001
verifies that the daemon runs on both workers and svc-2001 is Minted only on kerberator-eval-worker2 (1/1)

evals.prompt: Can you confirm svc-2001 only has tickets on the intended prod-a nodes?
expected: reads svc-2001's spec.nodeSelector {security-zone: prod-a}
lists which nodes match it (only kerberator-eval-worker)
compares that with per-node Principal status: Minted on kerberator-eval-worker; kerberator-eval-worker2 not Minted (pruned or skipped)
concludes targeting is correct and quotes 1/1 as eligible-node readiness
makes no change

evals.prompt: svc-2001's tickets disappeared from kerberator-eval-worker. Why?
expected: finds that svc-2001 is Ready=False with reason NoEligibleNodes
finds that its nodeSelector {security-zone: prod-a} now matches no node, because kerberator-eval-worker no longer has that label
explains that the daemon pruned the ticket when the node stopped matching, and that this is the intended fail-closed behaviour, not a daemon bug
suggests re-labelling the node (kubectl label node kerberator-eval-worker security-zone=prod-a) or changing the selector, as a command for the user
does not relabel the node or change the Principal without asking

evals.prompt: svc-2001 should be on every node again.
expected: finds the current restriction: spec.nodeSelector {security-zone: prod-a}
removes the Principal's nodeSelector entirely rather than labelling every node
does not remove the security-zone label from kerberator-eval-worker
waits and verifies that svc-2001 is Minted on both workers (2/2)
explains that 'every node' means every node the Tenant's daemon runs on (both workers, not the control-plane)
